p01.why: A goto may jump into a branch of an ordinary if, the condition is skipped, and r becomes 1.

p02.why: The initializer declares a = 3 and b = 4, the condition is false, and the else branch sees a and b and sets r to 7.

p03.why: extern is not allowed in a condition declaration.

p04.why: The then branch of if !consteval runs at run time and is not an immediate function context, so twice(v) with a non-constant v is invalid there.

p05.why: typedef is not allowed in a condition declaration.

p06.why: static is not allowed in a condition declaration.

p07.why: A condition declaration must not be a structured binding.

p08.why: a is visible only to the end of the if statement, so return a names nothing.

p09.why: Each else binds to the inner if, so the first statement sets r to 2 and the second does nothing.

p10.why: inline is not allowed in a condition declaration.

p11.why: 2 is a constant, and a conversion to bool that loses information is permitted in the if constexpr condition.

p12.why: constant has a constant initializer, so mode() is constant-evaluated and gives 1; mode() + offset is not a constant, so it runs at run time and gives 2.

p13.why: In a consteval function the then branch of if consteval always runs, so g() is 1.

p14.why: Both functions return 1 in the static_asserts; at run time, with the volatile sink stopping constant evaluation, each returns 2, so r is 4.

p15.why: case 1 jumps into the branch of if (false) and sets r to 7; case 0 skips the branch, so r stays 0.

p16.why: thread_local is not allowed in a condition declaration.

p17.why: A condition declaration must not declare an array.

p18.why: For int the t.size() branch is discarded and not instantiated, so size_of(Box{}) is 4 and size_of(3) is 1.

p19.why: The then branch of if consteval is an immediate function context, so twice(v) with non-constant v is valid there.

p20.why: A condition declaration must not declare a function.

p21.why: The outermost block of the then branch declares the condition variable x again.

p22.why: The generic lambda and the member of the local class in a template are templated contexts, and the discarded branches depend on the argument, so they are not instantiated; y is 0 and z is 2.

p23.why: An alias declaration is a valid initializer, and T is visible in the condition and the branch.

p24.why: A condition declaration must not define a class.

p25.why: Outside a template a discarded statement must still be valid, and undeclared_function is not declared.

p26.why: The outermost block of the else branch declares the condition variable x again.

p27.why: A goto from outside must not jump into a branch of if consteval.

p28.why: A block nested inside the branch may hide the condition variable.

p29.why: The initializer declares a constexpr n, so n > 1 is a constant expression.

p30.why: The branches add 1 and 1000, and the last if does nothing, so r is 1001.

p31.why: The else branch of if consteval must be a compound statement.

p32.why: A static_assert is not a valid initializer.

p33.why: A case label of the enclosing switch must not jump into a branch of if constexpr.

p34.why: Contextual conversion makes the null pointer and 0.0 false, &x, -3 and Flag{true} true, and allows the explicit operator bool, so hits is 3.

p35.why: The = {e} form is valid, x is 3 so r becomes 3, and the while condition y is 0 so the loop body never runs.

p36.why: A goto from outside must not jump into a branch of if constexpr, even the selected one.

p37.why: The else branch is a single declaration without braces that declares x again.

p38.why: The assignment sets x to 0, its value 0 converts to false, and main returns x, which is 0.

p39.why: The else branch of if !consteval is the constant-evaluation branch, so twice(v) is valid there.

p40.why: The outermost block of the branch declares the initializer's x again.

p41.why: if consteval must not have a condition in parentheses.

p42.why: The expression-statement initializer runs first, so n == 1 is true and main returns 0.

p43.why: The condition declares x again after the initializer declared it.

p44.why: p is one variable of pointer-to-function type with an initializer, which a condition may declare.

p45.why: Empty has no conversion to bool.

p46.why: The else if is a new if statement whose condition variable x is visible in its own else branch.

p47.why: A static variable, a class definition with a variable, and a function declaration are all valid initializers.

p48.why: ! after if must be followed by consteval.

p49.why: The constexpr explicit operator bool makes S{} a constant after contextual conversion.

p50.why: The then branch of if consteval must be a compound statement.

p51.why: Only the selected branch's return deduces the type, so pick<true> returns int and pick<false> returns double.

p52.why: The condition is evaluated one time, so calls is 1.

p53.why: x is 0 so the else branch sets seen to 0, y is 7 so seen becomes 7, and p is non-null so seen becomes 8.

p54.why: In a function that is not constexpr the then branch never runs, so where() returns 2.

p55.why: An empty statement is a valid initializer.

p56.why: The discarded return 2.0 does not take part in deduction, also outside a template, so f returns int.

p57.why: A condition declaration may use constexpr.

p58.why: The branch is its own scope even without braces, so y is not visible after the if.

p59.why: The address of a global is a constant and converts to true; the information-losing conversion is permitted.

p60.why: A condition declaration must have an initializer.

p61.why: A using-declaration is not a valid initializer.

p62.why: The condition temporary dies before the branch (x, B, a), and in the second statement c dies before a (B, c, a), giving xBaBca.

p63.why: never_declared() does not depend on T, so the discarded branch must be valid, and the name is not declared.

p64.why: A condition declaration must declare exactly one variable.

p65.why: b is a parameter, so the if constexpr condition is not a constant expression.

p66.why: A using-directive is not a valid initializer.

p67.why: never_defined is declared, so the discarded branch is valid, and a function used only there needs no definition.
